title: Simultaneous Fitting of Sigmoid Curves in Excel Using Solver
author: Kenji Ohgane
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8g9htz6

steps.title: Prepare Excel File and Data
steps.instruction: Download and open the 'ExcelSolver_SimultaneousFitting.xlsx' file and input your data into the designated 'x' and 'y' columns.

substeps.instruction: Ensure data in the 'x' column is in increasing or decreasing order to ensure correct plot display.

steps.title: Enter Initial Parameter Guesses
steps.instruction: Estimate and enter initial parameters (minimum, max, n, and ec_50) into the named cells based on the plot.

substeps.instruction: Enter values for the first data set in cells B2, B3, B4, and B5.
Enter values for the second data set in cells K2, K3, K4, and K5.
Modify equations within the 'ycalc' columns if the curve equations need adjustment.

steps.title: Configure Excel Solver
steps.instruction: Open the Solver add-in via Tool > Solver on the menu bar and configure the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Set 'Objective / Target cells' to $B$8 (Sum of Squared Residuals for both data sets).
Set the 'equal to' section to 'Value of 0' (ignore the 'unable to find solution' warning).

steps.title: Apply Solver Constraints
steps.instruction: Add specific constraints to the Solver to ensure biological and mathematical validity.

substeps.instruction: Add a constraint for 'ec_50 >= 0.000001' to prevent negative or zero values.
To share minimum and maximum values between the two curves, add constraints 'min = min_' and 'max = max_'.

steps.title: Run Solver and Validate Results
steps.instruction: Execute the Solver and evaluate the resulting fit.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Solve' and close the Solver window once the calculation is finished.
Retrieve the fitted parameters and verify that the sigmoid curves are reasonably fitted over the raw data points.
